definition: Testing one's abilities in a way that keeps one interested.
examples: My job as a divorce lawyer is very challenging.
It tests my abilities in a way that keeps me interested.

definition: Boring because of always doing exactly the same thing every day.
examples: Working as a checkout assistant can be a bit monotonous and repetitive.
I have to do exactly the same thing every day.

definition: Making you feel happy because it is useful and important.
examples: I'm a primary school teacher. I find working with children very rewarding.
It makes me happy because it's useful and important.

definition: Making you feel enthusiastic and willing to work hard.
examples: I work in a small design company and my job's really motivating.
I never mind having to work overtime.

definition: Requiring a lot of time, energy, or attention, often with high pressure.
examples: Being a surgeon is very demanding.
It's very high pressure and you have to work long hours.

definition: Really boring and making you feel impatient.
examples: I always wanted an exciting job, but sadly, mine is incredibly tedious.
It's really boring and it makes me feel impatient all the time.

definition: A job with low wages and no hope of promotion.
examples: He's in a dead-end job in the local factory.
The wages are low and there's no hope of promotion.

definition: Important and coming with a lot of responsibility.
translation: De alto nivel / De gran responsabilidad
examples: She's got a very high-powered job in finance.
It's important and comes with a lot of responsibility.

definition: An action you take to progress in your career.
examples: I'm hoping it'll be a good career move to go from publishing to advertising.

definition: The activity of trying to find a job.
examples: I've been unemployed for six months now, so I spend most of my time job hunting.

definition: A series of jobs from the lower paid with less responsibility to the highest paid with the most responsibility within a company.
examples: I'm a junior doctor, and if I want to move up the career ladder, I need to work in several different hospitals and departments.

definition: People who work for government departments.
examples: In Britain, people who work for government departments are called civil servants.

definition: A route or method which provides for more rapid results or promotion than usual.
examples: In some careers, people with very good qualifications are put onto a fast track so they get promoted more quickly.

definition: To voluntarily leave a job or other position.
examples: I've had enough of my job. I think I'm going to quit / resign.

definition: To lose your job because your employer no longer needs you.
examples: 400 workers have been laid off / made redundant.

definition: Without a paid job; unemployed.
examples: He's been out of work for nearly six months.

definition: Not working at a particular time, usually due to illness or holidays.
examples: He's been off work for nearly six months.

definition: To be removed from a job, usually for doing something wrong.
examples: She was sacked / was fired for refusing to work on Sundays.

definition: To be given a more important job or rank in the organization that you work for.
examples: Fantastic news! I'm going to get promoted!

definition: An advantage or something extra, such as money or goods, that you are given because of your job.
examples: The salary's a bit low, but we have some great perks / benefits.
